## Verdict
needs-revision

## Concerns
- The proposed projection repair is false under the stated definitions. Take
  \[
  \varphi=(n,r,i,j,a,b,N)=(6,3,2,2,1,2,2),\qquad \nu=(2,2,2).
  \]
  This tuple is valid and \(\nu\) is tall decomposable. In \(\operatorname{Lin}_{\varphi}(\nu)\), the coefficient of \(A_{\varnothing,(2)}\) is
  \[
  c_{(2,2),(2)}^{(2,2,2)}=1
  \]
  by Pieri. But \(C=(n-r-i)^j=(1)^2\), so the proposed \(P\) kills \(A_{\varnothing,(2)}\). Thus
  \[
  P(\operatorname{Lin}_{\widehat\varphi}(\widehat\nu))
  \ne \operatorname{Lin}_{\varphi}(\nu),
  \]
  contradicting the invoked Lemma 4.3 equality [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 777-788].
- Consequently, even embedded tall rows are not preserved by \(P\), and extending an original solution by zero need not solve the enlarged system. The large-\(N\) descent remains unproved.
- Therefore the requested target is **not established**. The conjugation map and parameter translation may remain conditionally sound, but the lower integral-basis theorem—and hence the right-adjoined theorem depending on it—has not received a valid proof audit.

## Unresolved certificates
- [proof-attempt] Replace the false projection step with a correct integral large-\(N\) descent: explicitly account for every original variable \(A_{\lambda,\theta}\) with \(\theta\subseteq(n-r)^r\), including the counterexample term \(A_{\varnothing,(2)}\), and prove that every solution of the original system extends to a solution of the enlarged system, or supply an alternative proof of the large-\(N\) inconsistency.
